Hydrogen ions (H⁺) are formed when a hydrogen atom loses its single electron, which is what happens when acids dissociate in water and release protons (these then bind to water as H₃O⁺). The team note about phosphocreatine breakdown is also relevant in a physiological context: that reaction consumes and releases ions in muscle, but it isn't the general way hydrogen ions form. I'm staying with the acid-dissociation answer as the general one.

CONFIDENCE: 66
